Items.Authors: Valentin Emberger, Luisa Ostler, Johannes Müller-Seidlitz, Wolfgang Treberer-Treberspurg, Astrid Mayr, Robert Andritschke, Annika Behrens, Günter Hauser, Peter Lechner, Leonie Sommer
Items.Title: Radiation effects and noise evolution in NewAthena WFI flight-production sensors
Items.Abstract: The Wide Field Imager (WFI), one of the two instruments aboard ESA’s upcoming large-class   X-ray observatory NewAthena, is optimized for imaging spectroscopy in the 0.2–15 keV energy range. Its focal plane comprises back-illuminated DEPFET sensors designed for high radiation tolerance. As part of the flight-production qualification, sensors were characterized to assess performance degradation induced by ionizing and non-ionizing radiation. The devices were irradiated with 62.4 MeV protons and 17.4 keV X-rays to total doses of   2.6E9 10-MeV-protons/cm² and 1.5 krad, respectively. We present the resulting changes in readout noise, dark current, and threshold voltage and compare them with the outcomes of a previous irradiation campaign on pre-flight devices. Implications for the required operating temperature and the expected end-of-life performance of the instrument are discussed.

Items.Authors: Fatima De Frondat Laadim, Julien Cailleux, Assia El Mouden, Nicola La Palombara, Jean-Laurent Dournaux, Giuseppe Leto, Cesare Molfese, Alessio Trois, Gianpiero Tagliaferri, Philippe Laporte, Hélène Sol, Andréas Zech, Alida Marchetti, Gianluca Giavitto, Richard White, Valentina Giordano, Fulvio Gianotti, Laura Proserpio, Giorgia Sironi, Gino Tosti, Ismam Abu, Claudio Arena, Carmelo Gargano, Pietro Giuseppe Bruno, William WANG, Salvatore Scuderi, Akira Okumura, James Anthony Hinton, Giovanni Pareschi, Christian Scaramozza, Simone Piras, Luca Trevisan, Alonda Sola-Molina, Connor Duffyk, Federico Russol Russol, Giovanni Lombardi, Laura Sarchi, Luigi Lessio, Primo Attinà, Rachele Millule, Samuel Branger, Simone Iovenittie, Valerio Pastorel, Vito Confortil
Items.Title: RAMS analysis of small-sized telescopes (SST) for CTAO
Items.Abstract: The Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) will be the world’s largest and most sensitive ground-based gamma-ray telescope array, with sites in La Palma, Spain, and the Atacama Desert, Chile. Its goal is to study high-energy cosmic phenomena such as black holes, pulsars, and supernova remnants by detecting Cherenkov radiation produced when gamma rays interact with the atmosphere. The Small-sized Telescopes (SST) will focus on the highest energy range.    Given CTAO’s 30-year lifetime and the harsh desert environment, the project demands exceptional Reliability, Availability, Maintainability, and Safety (RAMS), aiming for 98.5% telescope availability. This paper presents the SST RAMS analysis, detailing the methodology, tools, and maintenance strategies developed collaboratively to ensure high performance, minimize downtime, and meet stringent operational and cost requirements.

Items.Authors: Yue Sun, Teng Xu, Jiangfang Jiang, Wei Wei, Chao Liu, Xuhao Wu, Changyu Zeng, Tao Wang, Guohua Zhou, Hemin Sun, Xiaofei Li, Junzhe Huang, Hang Zhang, Massinissa Hadjara, Yonghui Hou
Items.Title: Recent developments of 100m-baseline optical/infrared interferometer in China
Items.Abstract: China's 100-meter baseline optical/infrared interferometer is approaching completion. It consists of three 600mm-aperture telescopes, with primary scientific objectives including conducting high-precision astrometry and performing high-resolution imaging observations of bright stars. The deployment and testing of the three telescopes are expected to be completed in 2026, enabling the first fringe observations. This paper presents the recent developments of the facility, including updates on the telescopes, vacuum pipelines, delay lines, beam combiners, beam stabilization systems, and the pilot observations using siderostats.

Items.Authors: Yaël Chich-Prunenec, Pierre Bourget, Nicolas Schuhler, Xavier Haubois, Johan Kosmalski
Items.Title: Removing the optical derotators in the Auxiliary Telescopes of the VLTI for enhanced astrometry and system performance
Items.Abstract: This initiative for the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI) involves removing the optical derotators from its Auxiliary Telescopes (ATs), which are currently used to compensate for the field-of-view rotation. The derotators introduce issues such as polarization-dependent visibility loss, optical throughput degradation, and operational complexity due to tight alignment requirements. Eliminating the derotators aims to enable astrometry along the north-south baseline, reduce visibility loss, and simplify operations. The project covers opto-mechanical design adaptations, simulations, and testing, ensuring system compatibility.

Items.Authors: Niranjan A. Thatte, Michele Cappellari, Dimitra Rigopoulou, Miguel Pereira-Santaella, Ismael Garcia-Bernete
Items.Title: Removing wiggles in JWST IFS data by forward-modelling the PSF
Items.Abstract: JWST NIRSpec and MIRI-MRS IFS use image slicers to remap the 2D light distribution at a given wavelength into a set of narrow slitlets, which are then dispersed to form the raw detector images. For NIRSpec, the incoming light is divided into 30 slitlets, each dispersed over ~2000 spectral pixels on two detectors. The raw frames encode intensity as a function of wavelength and position along each slitlet. For point sources, however, under-sampling prevents an accurate reconstruction of a regularly sampled 3D cube using standard methods. Our solution is a forward-modelling approach in the detector plane. We model the response of the unresolved point source at every detector pixel and subtract it directly from the raw 2D frames. We fit a single scale factor per wavelength to match the observed PSF footprint, and thus recover the point-source spectrum. The spectrum will be used to scale and subtract the PSF from each exposure, allowing the pipeline to produce a wiggle-free 3D cube.

Items.Authors: Nicholas Herrald, Francis Bennet, Michael Copeland, Ian Price, Elisa Jager, Grace McGinness, Christopher Stokes-Griffin
Items.Title: Reporting on the "Moon to Mars" optical communication system mechanical design
Items.Abstract: A laser communications system was developed at Mt Stromlo Observatory in Canberra, to be compatible with the Optical to Orion laser communication system on the Artemis II mission. A Planewave RC700 telescope is used to receive signals from the space-craft with a transmit system mounted as an outrigger. A simple and robust optical design was employed for both the transmit and receive systems. System design and resulting performance is described. Both transmit and receive systems have shown a high degree of target and alignment stability over time, across integration cycles, exceeding system requirements under challenging conditions including fully sunlit daytime operations.

Items.Authors: Yoshihiko Saito, Yoshimi Rokugawa, Kenta Sakabe, Hideki Takami
Items.Title: Research and development of adaptive optics for satellite-to-ground laser communications at NICT in Japan
Items.Abstract: The demand for laser satellite communications is increasing due to the need for secure, high-capacity data transmission. Current systems remain in the demonstration stage, with atmospheric turbulence posing a major challenge to signal stability. Adaptive optics and fine pointing systems are essential to mitigate these effects and ensure reliable satellite-to-ground links. In Japan, the National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT) has deployed multiple optical ground stations equipped with such technologies. This paper presents NICT’s progress in adaptive optics development and outlines future directions for expanding laser satellite communication infrastructure.

Items.Authors: Wei Wei, Teng Xu, Fanghua Jiang, Yue Sun, Chao Liu, Xuhao Wu, Hemin Sun, Changyu Zeng, Tao Wang, Junzhe Huang, Yonghui Hou
Items.Title: Research and test observation progress of terminal subsystems of the Chinese Optical Infrared 100 m-Long Baseline Interferometer
Items.Abstract: The infrastructure construction of the Chinese Optical Infrared 100m-Long Baseline Interferometer has been completed. At present, three 600 mm aperture telescopes are being adjusted inside the dome, and the overall debugging of the interferometer is expected to be completed in 2026. During this period, with the aid of two 150 mm aperture fixed sky mirror systems, the subsystems in the interferometric terminal, including tilt correction system, time-domain fringe detection system and observation strategy generation system, were tested on a 57 m baseline, and the fringes of the target celestial bodies were successfully captured. This paper will introduce research and test observation progress of the terminal subsystem of the interferometer.

Items.Authors: Enrique De Alba, Kimmy De Alba, Ryan Swindle, Justin Fletcher
Items.Title: Rethinking vision-first cloud detection in all-sky monitoring
Items.Abstract: Cloud detection from ground-based all-sky cameras is widely framed as a vision problem, with successive work pursuing more capable encoders. Whether this assumption holds at subregion granularity has not been directly tested. We evaluate three frozen encoder families alongside a baseline of curated statistical and metadata features and find all three converge to F1 scores between 0.81 and 0.82, while 15 observatory-derived features alone reach F1=0.87. Fusing frozen ResNet-50 embeddings with metadata does not significantly improve F1 but yields large gains in specificity (+0.08, p<0.001) and prevalence-aware normalized cost (-0.05, p<0.001), concentrating the visual channel's value in false-closure suppression. Our results suggest that metadata fusion and decision calibration yield larger returns than further backbone scaling under frozen extraction. More broadly, these findings caution against equating an image-based problem formulation with a vision-limited performance regime.

Items.Authors: Léonie Hoerner, Bruno Chazelas, Christophe Lovis, Nicolas Blind, Ludovic Genolet, Nathanael Restori, Ian Hughes, Michael Sordet, Robin Schnell, Samuel Rihs, Adrien Crausaz, David Ehrenreich, Emeline Bolmont, Christoph Mordasini, Martin Turbet, Maddalena Bugatti, Benoit Neichel, Thierry Fusco, Jean-François Sauvage, Isaac Bernardino Dinis, Angelie Alagao, Gilles Simond, Vincent Chambouleyron, Mathieu Motte, Anraud Striffling, Francisco oyarzun
Items.Title: RISTRETTO: assembly and testing of the seven-spaxel, high-resolution, diffraction-limited spectrograph
Items.Abstract: The RISTRETTO project aims at the direct detection of the reflected light of extra-solar planets to measure albedos and detect possible biosignatures, using the high-contrast / high-resolution method. We report on the assembly, lab-testing and on-sky testing of the seven-spaxel high-resolution single-mode spectrograph which was built ahead of the rest of the instrument.

Items.Authors: Cristian A. Rodriguez, Renate Kupke, Daren Dillion, Deno Stelter, Nicholas Mac Donald, Andy Skemer
Items.Title: SCALES spectrograph opto-mechanical design, manufacturing, and integration
Items.Abstract: Cryogenic infrared instruments inevitably face uncertainties in mechanical behavior during the transition from room temperature to operating temperature. Among the dominant effects are differential thermal contraction between dissimilar materials, micro-slip at mechanical interfaces, and distortion of parts arising from fabrication and material stresses. Cryogenic considerations aside, the size and performance requirements of the optics demanded extensive engineering to achieve manufacturability, structural rigidity, and stress-isolated mounting interfaces. This paper outlines the design strategies and manufacturing practices employed to minimise these effects and ensure reliable optical performance at operating temperature. These developments are for the spectrograph of the SCALES (Slicer Combined with an Array of Lenslets for Exoplanet Spectroscopy) instrument, a 2–5 μm coronagraphic integral field spectrograph currently under construction for the W. M. Keck Observatory.

Items.Authors: Francisco Javier Veredas, Sebastian Albrecht, Robert Andritschke, Andreas Lederhuber, Kirpal Nandra, Miriam Ramos-Ceja, Marko Mecina, Roland Ottensamer
Items.Title: Science and telemetry data format for the NewAthena WFI instrument
Items.Abstract: We present the trade-offs on the data format for the WFI NewAthena instrument. The data network limitations and architecture of the WFI hardware are illustrated in terms of science data size and data rate. A previous mission and configuration options, along with the science data format, are also presented. Our investigations revealed that data compression is necessary to meet the current data budget requirements. Improvements to the science package size settings are also considered before each observation to enhance data throughput.

Items.Authors: E. Arrigoni, S. Mereghetti, R. Campana, C. Labanti, A. Pisapia, P. Calabretto, G. Mattioli, E. Virgili, L. Amati
Items.Title: Scientific performances of the XGIS instrument on-board THESEUS
Items.Abstract: The XGIS is a dual camera coded mask hard X-ray instrument on-board the THESEUS satellite (proposed ESA M7 mission) designed to detect high-energy transients inside its wide FoV and accurately localise them to allow rapid follow-up observations. We present the expected XGIS scientific performance obtained thanks to MC simulations of the instrument and to imaging simulation using the synthetic population of GRB derived from theoretical studies and the currently proposed self-supporting mask pattern design.

Items.Authors: Lique Lin, Lu Li, Yousong Yue
Items.Title: SDE-CraterNet: a semantic detail-enhanced and context-aware framework for precise martian crater segmentation
Items.Abstract: Precise boundary detection of Martian craters is vital for understanding the geological evolution and supporting autonomous navigation. However, existing methods face major limitations including confusion with crater-like terrain, semantic misalignment during feature fusion, and blurred boundary identification.  Thereforte, this study proposes a semantic-detail-enhanced and context-aware crater segmentation framework. To improve the accuracy of crater boundary segmentation, a Semantic Detail-Enhanced Upsampling Module is proposed, which incorporates crater-specific detailed information from high-resolution feature maps and corrects the semantic misalignment induced by upsampling. To enhance the capability of discriminating craters from morphologically similar landforms, Swin Transformer i semployed as the backbone network, leveraging its inherent attention mechanism that exhibits high compatibility with the circular structural characteristics of craters.

Items.Authors: Stephen Guzzo, Keith Cummings
Items.Title: Second generation DKIST data handling system
Items.Abstract: The National Science Foundation’s Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST) is a 4-meter solar observatory in operation at Haleakalā, Hawaii. The DKIST Data Handling System (DHS) is responsible for capturing science data from instrument cameras as well as metadata from telescope systems. After data acquisition is complete, the DHS converts data and metadata to FITS format and facilitates off-site transfer to a data center in Boulder, Colorado. After DKIST entered operations at the end of 2021, the observatory routinely produced data contingents of tens of terabytes (TB) per day that were sent to the data center. In order to accommodate the integration of future instruments as well as larger and faster camera sensors, we undertook an effort to redesign the DHS to improve performance and increase storage space. In this paper, we describe the motivation for this overhaul, give descriptions of both the hardware and software designs, give performance results, and discuss future improvements.

Items.Authors: Nathan K. Long, Daniel S. Dahl, Christopher H. Betters, Julia J. Bryant, Nick Cvetojevic, Michael J. Ireland, Stefan Kraus, Sergio Leon-Saval, Frantz Martinache, Marc-Antoine Martinod, Barnaby Norris, Jyotirmay Paul, Akira Rodziewicz-Ryan, Adam K. Taras, Jin Wei, Peter G. Tuthill
Items.Title: Seidr update: photonic ‘black magic’ for high-contrast interferometry using kernel-nulling and photonic lanterns
Items.Abstract: Seidr is a new interferometric beam combiner within the Asgard Suite, utilizing infrastructure common to the Bifrost instrument at the Very Large Telescope Interferometer. Seidr combines hybrid mode-selective photonic lantern injection modules with a kernel-nulling photonic chip backend to enable deep H-band nulling for high-contrast studies of exoplanets, gravitational lensing events, and exomoons. This instrument update summarizes Seidr’s current design maturity and recent simulations of the point source – to – lantern outputs. We also outline progress on our neural network–based wavefront estimation scheme, which uses the photonic lantern outputs to sense phase fluctuations, designed to feed back to Baldr’s deformable mirror, and improve nuller light injection.

Items.Authors: Domenico Barbato, Jacopo Farinato, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Andrea Baruffolo, Federico Battaini, Maria Bergomi, Elena Carolo, Paolo Cerpelloni, Simonetta Chinellato, Valentina D'Orazi, Simone Di Filippo, Tania Sofia Gomes Machado, Davide Greggio, Fulvio Laudisio, Cecilia Lazzoni, Luigi Lessio, Alessandro Lorenzetto, Demetrio Magrin, Luca Marafatto, Lorenzo Merli, Dino Mesa, Lars Mohr, Manny Montoya, Davide Ricci, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Gabriele Umbriaco, Remon van Gaalen, Daniele Vassallo, Valentina Viotto
Items.Title: SHARK-NIR on the hunt: updates from early science runs and future horizons
Items.Abstract: SHARK-NIR is a near-infrared camera installed on the Large Binocular Telescope (LBT) in Arizona, performing high-contrast coronagraphic imaging, dual band imaging and low resolution spectroscopy in Y, J and H bands. Its main scientific goal is the search and characterization of exoplanets, exploiting the high performance of the LBT Adaptive Optics systems and synergic observations with SHARK-VIS (operating in V band) and LMIRCam (operating from K to M band) instruments on LBT.  Mounted on LBT in June 2022, SHARK-NIR first underwent a commissioning phase lasting until October 2023, aimed at testing its on-sky performance. An early-science phase followed, focusing on young exoplanets, protoplanetary disks, massive companions around accelerating stars and physical phenomena on minor bodies of the Solar System.  We present in this paper an updated description of SHARK-NIR, exploring its scientific output and the synergies with other instruments and exoplanetary detection methods.

Items.Authors: Bruce Lairson, James Tutt
Items.Title: Silicon carbide blocking filter grid geometries suitable for AXIS and newAthena
Items.Abstract: 4H-SiC single crystal X-ray grids have far higher strength and thermal conductance than the silicon used for XRISM grids. This results in X-ray blocking filters with higher strength and temperature uniformity, greatly mitigating issues such as launch durability and on-orbit signal decay. We present a design for a 76mm-aperture grid potentially suitable for the AXIS X-ray telescope, and a 128mm-aperture grid which could potentially be useful for the newAthena X-IFU entrance filter.

Items.Authors: Cyprien Lanthermann, Theo A. ten Brummelaar, Peter G. Tuthill, Narsireddy Anugu, E. Robert Ligon, Adam K. Taras, Grace Piroscia, J. Gordon Roberston, Gail Schaefer, Douglas R. Gies, Makoto Kishimoto
Items.Title: Silmaril: reducing the thermal background with a multi-stage narcissus mirror
Items.Abstract: Silmaril is a beam combiner at the CHARA Array designed for sensitivity, with the goal of reaching a limiting magnitude in the H- and K-band of 10. To reach this sensitivity in the K-band, we need to reduce the thermal background of the instrument, which is the dominant source of noise in K.  To do so, we use a Narcissus mirror, reflecting the thermal photons emitted by the cold camera (80 K) back to itself, except for the science beam going through specific holes placed in the mirror. In this presentation, we will describe the 2-stage design needed to overcome the physical limitations of the optical lab, and the design of the Narcissus mirrors to take into account the movement of the science beam pupils and the alignment process. We will then present the analysis of the resulting thermal-background reduction we obtain and compare it to the theoretical reduction of >90%.

Items.Authors: Klaus Subbotina Stephenson, Kate Jackson
Items.Title: Simulating Zernike-based CWFSing with HCIPy
Items.Abstract: This work covers the recent development of an open-source HCIPy-based simulation for curvature wavefront sensing (CWFS). Proceeding a brief introduction on CWFSing, the authors dive into the methodology behind their simulation efforts and discuss research regarding the best conjugation distances for CWFS planes according to the quantified ability to correct for discrete Zernike modes, per the relationship between spatial frequency and propagation distance from the pupil plane.

Items.Authors: Hui Kong, Jin Xu, Xiang Jiang, Ping Chen, Jialin Zhang, Fujia Du
Items.Title: Simulation method and implementation of autoguiding based on the Mutian telescope
Items.Abstract: To address long-duration tracking errors of the Mutian Telescope during observations caused by factors such   as periodic errors of ball bearings, small polar-axis deviations and gravitational deformation of the mounting   structure, this paper investigates the simulation and implementation of an autoguiding method. First, a simplified   tracking-error model is established based on the above errors, and a guide-star simulation program is constructed.   The ideal and actual positions of the guide-star image on the image plane are calculated from star-catalog   coordinates, telescope imaging parameters, and the error model. Simulated stellar images containing point   spread function (PSF) and noise characteristics are then generated to reproduce the low-signal-to-noise-ratio   output of the guide camera. In terms of image processing, an image-centroid extraction method combining the   centroid method, second-moment features, and two-dimensional Gaussian fitting is adopted. An inverse model

Items.Authors: Michela Todaro, Luisa Sciortino, Federico Fiorentino, Ugo Lo Cicero, Fabio D'Anca, Edoardo Alaimo, Tortorici Caterina, Pekka Törmä, Bahawal Haq, Matthew Soman, Pascal Mercère, Paulo Da Silva, Alfonso Collura, Salvatore Varisco, Claudio Saitta, Alberto Gulizzi, Gaspare Di Cicca, Gabriele Minervini, Elisabetta Cavazzuti, Daniele Brienza, Chiara Grappasonni, Simonetta Puccetti, Angela Volpe, Marco Barbera
Items.Title: Single- or multi-walled carbon nanotube pellicles investigated for NewAthena
Items.Abstract: CNT films are very promising as substrates for thermal and optical filters for X-ray or EUV detectors for space applications. This new technology is under evaluation as potential optical blocking and thermal filters for the ESA space mission New Athena. The main goal of this work is to compare the spectroscopic performance, in band (soft X-rays) and out-of-band (UV-VISMIR), of different kinds of CNT pellicles, namely randomly oriented dual layer single walled (SW), randomly oriented dual layer multi walled (MW), and oriented multiple layer MW. Based on this study, the appropriate CNT pellicle may be chosen to design a set of representative thin filter breadboards for the New Athena X-ray Integral Field Unit detector to achieve the Technology Readiness Level 5 before Athena Mission Adoption (June 2027).

Items.Authors: Robert Content, Yun Wang, Massimo Robberto, Gregory Wirth, Jon Lawrence, Lee Spitler, Mark Dickinson, Thomas Greene, Jeffrey Kruck, Will Percival, Andreas Faisst, Lynne Hillenbrand, Jeyhan Kartaltepe, Nikhil Padmanabhan, Lado Samushia, Lee Armus, Florian Beutler, Andrew Benson, Micol Bolzonella, Samuel Brieden, Jarle Brinchmann, Emanuele Daddi, Kyle Finner, Andrew Hearin, Cullan Howlett, Gregory Mosby, Eva-Maria Mueller, Seshadri Nadathur, Zoran Ninkov, Ken Osato, Casey Papovich, Jack Piotrowski, Lucia Pozzetti, Alvise Raccanelli, Jason Rhodes, Shun Saito, Hee-Jong Seo, Zachary Slepian, Stephen Smee
Items.Title: SIRMOS optical design: NIR spectroscopy of 100,000,000 galaxies at 1 < z < 4 and R~1300
Items.Abstract: SIRMOS (Satellite for Infrared Multi-Object Spectroscopy) is a NASA MIDEX mission concept to map the universe in 3D over ~500 cubic gigaparsecs using 100-million [OIII] and H-alpha emission line galaxies at 1< z<4. SIRMOS will probe the cosmic origin by placing constraints on primordial non-Gaussianity, precisely measure the sum of neutrino masses, and differentiate dark energy and modification of general relativity as the cause for the observed low-redshift cosmic acceleration. SIRMOS has a 60 cm aperture telescope with 0.9 square-degree field, and 2.2-million micromirrors on a digital micro-mirror devices (DMD) to provide a programmable reflective slit mask for spectroscopy at R~1300 over 1.25-2.5 microns. The multiplex advantage is 4000 even if the DMD is only 2048 micromirrors long. An alternate design uses a prism instead of a grating. Another uses a microshutter array instead of a DMD. The SIRMOS mission design is presented in a companion paper by Gregory Wirth.

Items.Authors: Johannes Wüthrich, Andrin Fazan, Sean MacBride, Marcelle Soares-Santos
Items.Title: Skipper CCD readout time optimization for astronomical applications
Items.Abstract: Skipper CCDs achieve noise reduction, relative to conventional CCDs, via repetitive measurements of pixel charge packets. However, this leads to an unavoidable increase in readout time, which often limits their application to astronomical instruments. To overcome this limitation, the optimal operation regime of Skipper CCDs must be determined, balancing noise improvement and readout time. We present a general optimization scheme derived from first principles and experimentally verified in the laboratory. Our results include analytical modeling of Skipper CCDs based on their intrinsic noise power spectral density, which allows the optimal operating point to be predicted rather than determined experimentally for each device. We further show that the location of this optimum is governed by the per-sample charge-transfer (skipper clocking) time. Finally, we present measurements that validate our results, using a Skipper CCD from the Oscura experiment.

Items.Authors: Ebru Uzunçam, Onur Şatır, Cihan Tuğrul Tezcan, Elif Köksal, Muhammed Baki Bayram, Bilal Arslan, Cahit Yeşilyaprak
Items.Title: Sky coverage statistics for DAG400 Telescope: natural guide star availability
Items.Abstract: This work focuses on the natural guide star (NGS) sky coverage for the 4-m DAG400 Telescope as it enters first light and primary operations. Since adaptive optics (AO) performance depends on finding an NGS of sufficient brightness within the required field of view, a statistical approach is used to determine practical limits. We analyze the probability of locating stars brighter than specific magnitude thresholds for the TROIA AO system; a flexible concept that adjusts corrected modes to atmospheric conditions and NGS brightness.

Items.Authors: Louis Gabarra, F. Cogato, M. Kuljanac, E. Medinaceli, K. Paterson, M. Schirmer
Items.Title: Snowballs detection in Euclid/NISP
Items.Abstract: Since its launch in July 2023, the Euclid mission has been operating successfully, although its scientific observa-  tions are affected by detector artefacts that must be accurately characterised to minimise their impact on data  analysis. In this work, we investigate one such class of transient events affecting the Near Infrared Spectrometer  and Photometer (NISP) instrument and its sixteen H2RG detectors, referred to as snowballs. These highly  energetic events produce compact saturated regions and long-lived persistence signals that can contaminate both  imaging and slitless spectroscopic observations. We present the NISP Cosmic Rays And Snowballs Identifier  (CRASI), a software toolkit that detects, classifies, and characterises transient detector events using only the  reconstructed science signal and quality factor maps generated by the NISP onboard processing.

Items.Authors: Laurel ONeill, Abraham Falcone, David M. Palmer, Md. Arman Hossen, Kadri Nizam, Lukas Stone, Ian Ashcroft, Brynn Bortree, Sierra Deppe, Timothy Emeigh, Killian Gremling, Gavin Houlihan, Katie McWhirter, Abigail Raytsis
Items.Title: Source centroiding and angular resolution with BlackCAT and beyond
Items.Abstract: The Black hole Coded Aperture Telescope (BlackCAT) CubeSat. BlackCAT is a 6U CubeSat developed by the Pennsylvania State University optimized for the detection of high-redshift gamma-ray bursts (GRB), the detection of high-energy transient events, and detection and localization of electromagnetic counterparts to gravitational wave events. X-ray source centroiding of data from the Black hole Coded Aperture Telescope CubeSat and its angular resolution are discussed. The impacts and potential improvements from sub-pixel event repositioning will be discussed, as well as preliminary designs of a “mesh experiment” to investigate sub-pixel event localization and charge spreading.

Items.Authors: Pavel Shchekaturov, Bogdan Jeram, Christian Soenke, Linus Karl, Claudio Reinero, Robert Donaldson, Pablo Burgos, Cristian Herrera
Items.Title: SPARTA upgrade RTC: status overview
Items.Abstract: “SPARTA Upgrade” is an obsolescence-mitigation project for the Standard Platform for Adaptive Optics Real-Time Control (SPARTA) Hard Real-Time Computer (HRTC), used on existing VLT instruments. Its goal is to replace the ageing platform with the latest high-performance COTS servers, combining new hardware technologies with modern real-time software programming techniques developed for the ELT, in order to achieve required performance.    The HRTC upgrade for existing systems such as AOF (GALACSI, GRAAL) and ERIS includes the replacement of the FPGA-based RTX box with a dual-socket Dell high-performance server based on modern multi-core AMD CPU architecture, the re-implementation of the SPARTA real-time core software, and an upgrade of the I/O hardware to modern PCIe cards while maintaining the sFPDP interfaces to the existing WFS cameras and DSM, and keeping the interfaces to the SPARTA co-processing cluster unchanged.

Items.Authors: A. Altmann, R. Andritschke, V. Antonelli, T. F. Bechteler, V. Burwitz, D. Fink, C. Fiorini, M. Goretti, P. Knopp, P. Lechner, N. Meidinger, J. W. Muegge, C. Sandow, R. Strecker
Items.Title: Spectroscopic performance of the electrical functional models for the eXTP SFA-T detectors
Items.Abstract: The Spectroscopy Focusing Array (SFA) is one of the three instruments on the eXTP satellite. It consists of six telescopes plus focal plane cameras, where five are equipped with a Silicon Drift Detector (SDD). These five SFA-T (T stands for timing) instruments are used for observations with high time resolution (≤ 10 µs), high throughput (dead time ≤ 5 % when observing a 1 Crab source), and good energy resolution (≤ 180 eV at 6 keV).  This paper presents the spectroscopic performance of the three Electrical Functional Models (EFM) for SFA-T that are assembled and tested at the Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics (MPE). A focus lies on the energy resolution at the planned sensor operating temperature of -45 °C after optimization of the SDD bias voltages.

Items.Authors: Hui Wang, Jiaben Lin, Mingfu Shao, Liyue Tong, Chen Yang
Items.Title: Spot-classification: a benchmark dataset for fine-grained solar magnetic topology
Items.Abstract: Accurate sunspot classification is vital for space weather forecasting. We present JW-SSD, a multimodal benchmark for fine-grained sunspot magnetic classification. Derived from SDO/HMI SHARP data (2010–2023), it comprises 36,553 magnetogram–continuum pairs from 2,507 active regions. Unlike conventional 3-class schemes, JW-SSD refines the Mount Wilson classification into five categories (α, β, β-δ, β-γ, β-γ-δ) to better characterize magnetic complexity. Rigorous quality control ensures high data validity. The dataset provides FITS/PNG formats with standard train/test splits. An improved U-Net baseline achieves 89.42% (3-class) and 88.15% (5-class) accuracy. Furthermore, JW-SSD successfully trains JW-SunSpot, a multimodal large language model, demonstrating its broad applicability for both conventional and large-model approaches.

Items.Authors: Peter Marley Chingaipe, Gyorgy Medgyesi, Alexandra Mazzoli, Emilie Bouzerand, Romain Laugier, Péter Ábrahám, Colin Dandumont, Denis Defrère, Adrian Glauser, Germain Garreau, Michael Ireland, András Joó, Jérôme Loicq, Marc-Antoine Martinod, Kwinten Missiaen, Manny Montoya, Johan Morren, Gert Raskin, Muhammad Salman, Warrick Schofield, Wannes Verstraeten
Items.Title: Status and performance of the Asgard/NOTT cold nulling camera
Items.Abstract: The Nulling Observations of dusT and PlaneTs (NOTT) instrument, part of the Asgard suite, will be the first nuller on the Very Large Telescope Interferometer (VLTI). Using long-baseline nulling interferometry in the L′-band (3.5–4.0 μm), NOTT suppresses stellar light to enable high-contrast imaging of exoplanets and circumstellar dust at high angular resolution. Its primary science goals include characterising hot/warm exozodiacal dust and detecting young Jupiter-like exoplanets at close (<10 AU) orbital separations. By combining light from up to four VLTI telescopes, NOTT will open new pathways for studying planetary formation environments and giant planet populations.

Items.Authors: Fabrizio Fornasiero, Luca Oggioni, Giorgio Pariani, Samuel Ronayette
Items.Title: Straylight characterization and performance assessment for Phase A of the THESEUS mission
Items.Abstract: The THESEUS mission is a proposal for ESA’s M7 call and is currently undergoing Phase A assessment. The InfraRed Telescope (IRT), part of the mission payload, is an infrared instrument based on a Three-Mirror Anastigmat (TMA) design. In this work, we evaluate the impact of both in-field and out-of-field stray light. The primary sources of stray light are identified within the context of the mission, and their effects are quantified through empirical analysis and numerical simulations. The baffle geometry is optimized within the allocated envelope, and numerical simulations performed with FRED Optical are compared against theoretical models.

Items.Authors: Stefan J. Wijnholds, Tammo Jan Dijkema, Sarod Yatawatta
Items.Title: Streaming visibility processing for large radio interferometers
Items.Abstract: The temporal and spectral resolution of the raw visibility data of a radio interferometer is usually driven by the need to limit time and frequency smearing on the longest baseline and by measures to flag or remove interfering signals. Initial processing usually involves steps like flagging and (baseline-dependent) averaging, reducing the visibility data volume significantly. Streaming visibility processing (SVP) avoids intermediate storage of the (uncompressed) raw visibility data. This relaxes the requirements on the storage buffer size and access performance, thereby reducing its costs and permitting a more energy efficient solution. In this contribution, we present an SVP solution that we demonstrate with the ALMA correlator emulator and the LOFAR correlator. We also demonstrate that SVP enables near real-time processing by showing results from a low-latency imager for quality assurance in ALMA observations.

Items.Authors: Takumi Togashi, Shuichi Gunji, Keito Watanabe, Haruaki Niinuma, Natsuki Kurooka, Daisuke Yonetoku, Tatsuya Sawano, Mutsumi Sugizaki, Makoto Arimoto, Hatsune Goto, Isshin Nagataka, Akihiro Doi, Hideo Matsuhara, Yoshimoto Maeda, Daiki Ishi, Hiroshi Tomida, Takanori Sakamoto, Motoko Serino, Tatehiro Mihara, Yusuke Kono, Hiroshi Akitaya, Hiroyuki Uchida
Items.Title: Study of detection algorithm for high-redshift GRBs to be observed by HiZ-GUNDAM/EAGLE
Items.Abstract: HiZ-GUNDAM is a future astronomical satellite mission aimed at exploring the early Universe through observations of high-redshift gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). The satellite will carry the wide-field X-ray monitor EAGLE and the optical/near-infrared telescope MONSTER. To enable follow-up observations with MONSTER, the source position needs to be localized with an accuracy better than 3′. To achieve this goal, we developed an EAGLE observation simulator and used it to study algorithms for transient-source detection and localization. The EAGLE response was calculated using Geant4, and the X-ray sky was modeled using ROSAT All-Sky Survey data and known source catalogs. Using these models, we simulated high-redshift GRBs at various positions within the EAGLE field of view and evaluated the current detection and localization algorithms. The results demonstrate that a localization accuracy of approximately 1.04′ can be achieved for GRBs with fluxes greater than 7 × 10⁻¹⁰ erg cm⁻² s⁻¹.

Items.Authors: Nicolò Azzaroli, Runa A. Briguglio, Marco Xompero, Pietro Ferraiuolo, Luca Oggioni, Giorgio Pariani, Armando Riccardi, Chiara Selmi
Items.Title: Subaperture calibration of deformable mirror for ELT-era DM size
Items.Abstract: In the VLT era, adaptive optics (AO) provided a major performance boost, but in the ELT era it has become essential. As primary mirrors grow, deformable mirrors (DMs) must also increase in size, requiring larger and more complex calibration facilities. Convex secondary DMs add further challenges, demanding larger optical beams for testing. This paper presents, to our knowledge, the first DM calibration performed in sub-aperture mode, where the mirror is never viewed in full clear aperture during calibration. This method enables the use of more compact and cost-effective test facilities, simplifying design, manufacturing, assembly, and calibration processes.

Items.Authors: Nicholas E. Thomas, Hugo Allaire, Jeffrey Apple, Adrianah Appleman, Dhamar Astilla Munoz, Aya Bamba, Stephen Bongiorno, McKinley Brumback, Patrick Champey, Chien-Ting Chen, Renata Cumbee, Kirtankumar P. Dixit, Steven Ehlert, Gen Fujimoto, Jessica Gaskin, Danielle Gurgew, Anthony Guillory, Kouichi Hagino, Iroha Ichiseki, Philip Kaaret, Nicholas Kafkoulas, Miho Katsuragawa, Fabian Kislat, Jeffery Kolodziejczak, Henric Krawczynski, Ioannis Liodakis, W. Peter Maksym, Kaya Mori, Shunsaku Nagasawa, Brian Ramsey, Daniel Radomski, Panini Singam, Patrick Slane, Chet Speegle, Douglas Swartz, Tadayuki Takahashi, Shin’ichiro Takeda, Shin Watanabe
Items.Title: SuperHERO x-ray telescope balloon mission
Items.Abstract: The SuperHERO hard X-ray telescope will observe extended sources at unprecedented imaging resolution, revealing the origins of non-thermal emission in extreme astrophysical environments. Employing NASA Marshall Space Flight Center’s replicated NiCo full-shell X-ray mirror technology to achieve better than 10-arcsecond half-power diameter (HPD) angular resolution on a balloon platform, SuperHERO consists of seven identical, co-aligned telescopes with a combined effective area of 45 cm² at 30 keV. SuperHERO was selected in the APRA 2023 call as a five-year mission, with an inaugural two-day flight scheduled from Fort Sumner, New Mexico, in the fall of 2028. For its initial target, SuperHERO will observe the Crab pulsar wind nebula, localizing hard X-ray emission. Mission development is currently underway, with updates and status to be provided in this presentation.

Items.Authors: Hangjian Liu, Bowen Yang, Xiangyi Gao, Danpei Zhao
Items.Title: Supervised deep PSF modeling for wide-field telescope imaging with scarce calibration stars
Items.Abstract: The imaging quality of stars over a large field of view is fundamentally limited by the modeling accuracy of the point spread function (PSF). Most existing approaches are designed for small fields and degrade in challenging regimes such as sparse star fields, crowded regions, and coronagraphic occlusion, where suitable PSF calibration stars are scarce. We propose a deep PSF-aware image enhancement framework. First, a supervised learning module learns a spatially varying wide-field PSF, thereby overcoming traditional small-field limitations. Second, a PSF posterior correction module is devised, which adaptively tunes the estimation strategy to alleviate model degradation. Experiments conducted on the self-constructed simulation dataset demonstrate that this method significantly improves the PSF estimation accuracy, and outperforms the standard pipeline in both robustness and speed of star map matching.

Items.Authors: Shouwei Hu, Dehua Yang, Liang Chen, Cheng Liu
Items.Title: Support system design of the tertiary mirror of the 4m JUST telescope
Items.Abstract: The Jiaotong University Spectroscopic Telescope (JUST) is a large optical telescope that requires a high-precision elliptical tertiary plano mirror. The support design of the mirror is crucial for its performance and stability. In this paper, we propose a novel support design method that combines lightweighting, 18 point whiffle-tree, and optimization techniques. We use finite element analysis to model the mirror and its support system, and optimize the parameters of the whiffletree to minimize the deformation and stress of the mirror. We conclude that our method is feasible and effective for the support design of the elliptical tertiary plano mirror of the JUST.

Items.Authors: Yanlyu Yang, Xiaofei Li, Xin He, Hua Bai, Dehua Yang, Xiangqun Cui
Items.Title: System analysis of the 4m segmented JUST telescope
Items.Abstract: The Jiaotong University Spectroscopic Telescope (JUST) a 4-m class telescope with the primary mirror segmented into 18 hexagonal sub-mirrors. This work develops an integrated system model that couples structural and optical performance analysis. A lean finite element model of the telescope, incorporating the simplified segmented mirror and support structure, was built to evaluate gravitational deflection, modal characteristics, and dynamic responses to wind and seismic loads. The resulting deformation fields were then reduced to piston and tip/tilt errors of the primary segments, secondary and the tertiary mirror and transferred to Zemax through a dedicated data-exchange interface. The telescope’s tracking and pointing accuracy was furtherly analyzed via induced aberrations. The fully coupled mechanical-optical model enabled direct propagation of perturbations into the optical system to evaluate final image quality and better understand telescope performance during design.

Items.Authors: Davide Vaccaro, Emanuele Taralli, Martin de Wit, Luciano Gottardi, Paul van der Hulst, Jan van der Kuur, Tobias Vos, Joseph S. Adams, Simon Bandler, Douglas Bennett, James Chervenak, Bertrand Doriese, Malcolm Durkin, Johnathon D. Gard, Carl Reintsema, Kazuhiro Sakai, Stephen Smith, Joel Ullom, Nicholas Wakeham, Roland H. den Hartog, Brian Jackson, Pourya Khosropanah, Aurora Simionescu
Items.Title: System performance of the sensor-readout chain in the FPA-DM for NewAthena X-IFU
Items.Abstract: The X-ray Integral Field Unit (X-IFU) of ESA’s Athena observatory is designed to deliver high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy with 2.5 eV energy resolution up to 7 keV and 5″ spatial resolution across the 0.2-12 keV band, using an array of 1500 TES with TDM readout. As part of our responsibility for the focal plane assembly (FPA), at SRON we have integrated and validated the sensor-readout chain for the X-IFU Demonstration Model (FPA-DM1.1), based on components delivered by VTT Finland, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) and by the National Institute of Standard and Technology (NIST).  In this contribution we present the first full sensor–readout chain performance characterization at system level of the FPA-DM1.1, which uses 4 TDM channels with 34 physical pixels each, operated in a TDM timing configuration representative of the flight baseline of 48-row multiplexing, which provides a co-added spectral performance at a level of 2.2 eV measured at 6 keV.

Items.Authors: Igor Petrucci, Carlos Lahoz, Diogo Batista, Daniel Bednarski
Items.Title: Systems thinking applied to the safety of the GMACS instrument for the Giant Magellan Telescope
Items.Abstract: This paper describes the application of the System-Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA), grounded in the STAMP framework, to the design and operation of GMACS, a large scale astronomical multi object spectrograph for the Giant Magellan Telescope. Unlike traditional component centric methods, STPA reconceptualizes safety as a control problem arising from unsafe interactions among hardware, software, procedures, and human operators. The analysis focuses on the Mask Exchange Mechanism, a critical subsystem enabling rapid and precise replacement of slit masks during spectroscopic observations. Because this mechanism involves tightly coupled mechanical, software, and human elements, inadequate coordination or unsafe control actions could result in performance losses, equipment damage, or risks to personnel.

Items.Authors: Bortolino Saggin, Marco Giovanni Corti, Luca Oggioni, Marco Riva, Diego Scaccabarozzi, Luca Terenzi
Items.Title: Telescope design of the IRT instrument
Items.Abstract: The design of the IRT telescope has been carried-out during the phase A study of the Theseus mission. The reference IRT operation includes a slew maneuver from the S/C attitude adopted during the survey mode to the one needed to follow identified GRB sources, this in general creates a change in the environmental heat fluxes both on the telescope and the S/C determining a thermal transient. The main challenge in the IRT telescope design is therefore granting the optical performances throughout these thermal transients. The telescope design is based on a Korsch optical scheme identified during a previous study, with a 700 mm primary mirror diameter and a focal length of about 6 m. The preliminary tradeoff on materials have led to the combination of low CTE materials both for the optical elements and the structural ones i.e. Zerodur and mostly carbon fiber reinforced epoxy.

Items.Authors: Shi-hao Wang, Hong-fei Zhang, Feng Zeng, Yi-Cheng Lin, Xing-bo Wang, Jian Wang
Items.Title: Temperature control system for scientific camera based on multistage TEC
Items.Abstract: Scientific cameras are essential instruments in astronomy, biological fluorescence imaging, and quantum physics due to their high sensitivity. However, the performance of high-end CMOS/CCD sensors is often limited by thermally generated dark current. To suppress this noise without introducing the vibration associated with mechanical cryocoolers, this paper presents a digital temperature control system based on a multi-stage Thermoelectric Cooler (TEC). The system features a hybrid driving architecture that combines the efficiency of a DC-DC converter with the low-noise characteristics required for precision imaging. By utilizing a 4-stage TEC assembly driven by a linearly adjustable voltage source (TPS40056 controlled via DAC), the design eliminates the switching noise interference typical of direct PWM drivers. The control logic, implemented on an STM32 microcontroller using a digital PID algorithm, achieves precise thermal regulation.

Items.Authors: Sebastiano Ligori, Leonardo Corcione, Vito Capobianco, Donata Bonino, Mauro Focardi, Anna M. Di Giorgio, Shige John Liu, Navin K. Shivapa Kamble
Items.Title: The application software for the instrument control unit of the Ariel mission: design and testing approach
Items.Abstract: In this paper we present the current status of the development of the application software of the Instrument Control Unit of the Ariel mission, which has the objective to obtain spectra for a number of transiting exoplanets. The Instrument Control Unit provides Command and Control functionalities for the AIRS spectrograph and the Telescope Control Unit, which is used to control and move the secondary mirror mechanism and provides the telescope temperatures.  We will illustrate the main functionalities of the software as well as the approach we are using for testing at different level, from static analysis to unit tests, to functional tests.

Items.Authors: Jyotirmay Paul, Daniel Lancaster, Sorabh Chhabra, Stefan Kraus, Michael Ireland, Owain Snaith, John Monnier, Daniel Ahrer
Items.Title: The Asgard/BIFROST pre-injection optics and fibre injection module: revision of optomechanical design and lab and on sky results
Items.Abstract: The Asgard/BIFROST instrument at the VLTI will enable high-spectral-resolution interferometry across 1.0 µm (Y, J, H bands). Its pre-injection optics correct for birefringence and longitudinal dispersion, while the fibre-injection module compresses beams into single-mode fibres. A fibre-switching module allows injection into photonic devices optimized for different wavebands. We present a comprehensive revision of the optical and optomechanical design, including redesigned mounting interfaces, refined pupil positioning, and enhanced mechanical stability to improve alignment strategy and fibre-coupling efficiency. Laboratory characterization shows significant gains in efficiency, stability, and repeatability, with on-sky commissioning results to be presented. The upgraded system provides a stable, high-throughput system to the Asgard/BIFROST.

Items.Authors: Saverio Lombardi, Fabrizio Lucarelli, Fabio Pintore, Lucio Angelo Antonelli, Ciro Bigongiari, Andrea Bulgarelli, Milvia Capalbi, Martina Cardillo, Fausto Casaburo, Francesco Casini, Antonio Alessio Compagnino, Vito Conforti, Silvia Crestan, Giancarlo Cusumano, Antonino D'Aì, Olena Fedorova, Federico Fiordoliva, Luca Foffano, Stefano Gallozzi, Stefano Germani, Andrea Giuliani, Simone Iovenitti, Antonino La Barbera, Valentina La Parola, Teresa Mineo, Edgar Molina, Davide Mollica, Antonio Pagliaro, Giovanni Pareschi, Nicolò Parmiggiani, Valerio Pastore, Francesco Gabriele Saturni, Salvatore Scuderi, Gino Tosti, Stefano Vercellone, Georgios Zacharis, Luca Zampieri
Items.Title: The ASTRI Mini-Array project data processing system: main components, functionalities, and interfaces
Items.Abstract: The ASTRI Mini-Array Project, led by INAF, is building nine 4-m class Cherenkov telescopes at the Teide Observatory, Spain. Seven telescopes are already installed, with two of them currently undergoing the commissioning and science verification phase.  The ASTRI project features the data processing system (DPS), a dedicated system for the end-to-end data processing and scientific exploitation. Raw data are immediately transferred from on site to the ASTRI data center in Rome (Italy) via high-speed network. The DPS employs a multi-stage pipeline on a HPC cluster to perform data pre-processing, calibration, reduction, and analysis, aiming for fast, reliable, and reproducible generation of science-ready products (event-lists and IRFs) and preliminary science products.  This contribution overviews the main DPS components, functionalities, and interfaces, and presents results from its current development and testing using commissioning data of the first group of telescopes in the array.

Items.Authors: B. Wehbe, A. Cabral, J. Delorme, P. Pereira, N. Blind, C. Lovis
Items.Title: The atmospheric dispersion corrector of RISTRETTO: a closed-loop concept
Items.Abstract: With the complexity of new instruments like RISTRETTO, it is essential to simplify how an ADC works and how we will guarantee satisfaction with the requirements. A new simple method is proposed for the case of RISTRETTO. In this paper, we will present the concept behind this closed-loop concept, as well as the preliminary design of the ADC.

Items.Authors: Claudio Macculi, Matteo D'Andrea, Lorenzo Ferrari Barusso, Giacomo Gorla, Simone Lotti, Gabriele Minervini, Francesco Monastra, Luigi Piro, Marcello Celasco, Flavio Gatti, Daniele Grosso, Manuela Rigano, Fabio Chiarello, Guido Torrioli, Mauro Fiorini, Michela C. A. Uslenghi, Daniele Brienza, Elisabetta Cavazzuti, Chiara Grappasonni, Simonetta Puccetti, Angela Volpe, Paolo Bastia, Artur Cardoso Coimbra, Francesco Villa
Items.Title: The cryogenic anticoincidence detector for the Athena X-IFU instrument: status towards the TRL5
Items.Abstract: The Cryogenic AntiCoincidence detector (CryoAC) is a particle detector aimed at increasing the X-IFU instrument sensitivity, a cryogenic TES microcalorimeter on-board the Athena mission, the next ESA X-ray Large mission planned for the Adoption in early 2027. Athena will host two complementary instruments optimized for energy resolution and FoV: the X-IFU and the WFI. The X-IFU main TES array detector, a high-grade imaging spectrometer, cannot distinguish among in-band energy depositions from charged particles crossing its absorbers, the Non X-ray Background (NXB), and the X-ray photons that make the scientific signal. The CryoAC will detect these charged particles thus enabling NXB level of 5E-3 cts/cm2/s/keV. It is a 4-pixel TES based microcalorimeter detector operating at 50 mK developed by an Italian team made by ASI, INAF, Genova University and CNR/IFN Roma. In this contribution we present the current status of CryoAC development toward TRL5, and outline the programmatic roadmap.

Items.Authors: Claire Juramy, Pierre Antilogus, Pierre Astier, John Banovetz, Sean Patrick MacBride, Andrew P. Rasmussen, Yousuke Utsumi
Items.Title: The dark dips phenomenon in the LSST camera on-sky images
Items.Abstract: When the LSST Camera started taking on-sky images at the Vera Rubin Observatory, some of the ITL STA3800 CCDs exhibited a previously undocumented effect. When a sufficiently bright star is superimposed over the sky background, the sensor columns that contain the star appear slightly darker than the background, both above and below the position of the star. This effect is not uniform across sensors, reaching an amplitude of up to seven percent of the background in the worst cases, but being undetectable in other sensors. For the affected sensors, the threshold required for the dips to become detectable also varies, from a few hundreds to a few thousands saturated pixels.

Items.Authors: Mariachiara Celato, Paul Hedderman, Christoph Tenzer, Andrea E. Santangelo, Hannah Lerman, Melissa McHugh, Ian Hutchinson, Paul T. O'Brien
Items.Title: The data processing pipeline for the THESEUS soft x-ray imager
Items.Abstract: The THESEUS mission is designed to detect Gamma-Ray Bursts, X-ray transients, and infrared afterglows in order to probe the high-redshift Universe and advance time-domain and multi-messenger astrophysics. Its scientific capabilities rely on a coordinated payload, including the Soft X-ray Imager (SXI). This contribution presents the SXI data-processing pipeline developed during the ESA M7 Phase A study. The SXI consists of two wide-field lobster-eye cameras covering the 0.3 to 5 keV energy band and producing high-speed data streams that require efficient onboard processing. We outline the detection and imaging chain, describe the modelling of the lobster-eye PSF and the localisation method, and detail the logic and expected performance of the onboard transient trigger algorithm.
